name: WHIST
description: Whist is the classic English partnership trick-taking game and ancestor of Bridge. 4 players, 2 teams. 52 cards, 13 each. Last card dealt (to dealer) turned face-up = trump. Eldest hand leads. Follow suit. Each trick over 6 = 1 point. Honours (A-K-Q-J of trump): 3 held = 2pts, 4 held = 4pts. Game to 5 (British) or 7 (American). Rubber = best of 3.

content.text: Whist is the classic English partnership trick-taking game and ancestor of Bridge. 4 players, 2 teams. 52 cards, 13 each. Last card dealt (to dealer) turned face-up = trump. Eldest hand leads. Follow suit. Each trick over 6 = 1 point. Honours (A-K-Q-J of trump): 3 held = 2pts, 4 held = 4pts. Game to 5 (British) or 7 (American). Rubber = best of 3.

Whist originated in 17th–18th century England, evolving from Ruff and Honours (described in The Complete Gamester, 1674). Played with a full 52-card pack, it superseded its predecessor in the 18th century. The name derives from the period word meaning quiet or attentive. It was first played on scientific principles at London's Crown Coffee House (c. 1728); Edmond Hoyle's 1742 treatise became the standard for a century.
13 each. Last card (to dealer) turned up = trump.
